title: Research sprint goal: kb/_self explains the agent coordination tooling in one owner doc
goal: Read on origin/main the code each part of the planned kb/_self/coordination.md describes (_tools/coord.py, .claude/hooks/coord_hook.py, _tools/kbask.py, .claude/agents/kb-observer.md, the coord_ tools of _tools/kb_mcp.py and KB_COORD_TOOLS, _tools/mon_coord.py with the kbmon panels that read coord, the own records and safe_to_remove of _tools/bl_clean.py, the coord rows of the benchmarks in kb/_self/reports/ and kb/_self/token-efficiency.md, and each tool's Windows path), and record in this story's notes, per part of the doc, the facts with their file:line; each place where monitoring.md, tools.md, plugin.md, benchmarks.md or token-efficiency.md says what the code does not do is filed as a draft bug with a failing repro and named in the notes; the notes end with `No outside facts: the goal describes this project's own tools, read from their code`, since no kb root's article changes.

gates.question: Where do the per-part facts with their file:line live, when a notes field holds 2000 characters at most (TEXT_MAX) and the facts run to about 23000?
options: one link of the story for each part or half part, a summary and the bug list in notes
gates.recommendation: one link of the story for each part or half part, a summary and the bug list in notes
gates.answer: one link of the story for each part or half part, a summary and the bug list in notes

Research part 1 (coord.py store and commands), 1 of 4, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- One SQLite file with two tables: entries(key, value, revision, holder, token, ttl, expires, budget) and events(seq autoincrement, kind, fields JSON, at) (_tools/coord.py:141-148). It opens with a 30 s busy timeout in autocommit mode (_tools/coord.py:135, :188-193) and every write is one BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction (_tools/coord.py:196-210); the clock is read after the lock is held, so a lease runs its full length (_tools/coord.py:312, :813-815).
- Store path: --store, else KB_COORD_STORE, else kb-coord/coord.sqlite in the common git directory of the clone that holds the script, which the clone's worktrees share (_tools/coord.py:1163, :1133-1136, :1117-1130); where git cannot run it reads .git itself (_tools/coord.py:1096-1114); a script in no git clone with neither is refused, exit 2 (_tools/coord.py:1164-1167).
- claim: the key is an id of 1 to 120 characters of letters, digits and _ . : / # @ - (_tools/coord.py:155, :301-302); --budget only for a backlog item id (_tools/coord.py:305-308); the token is 32 hex characters, shown once to the claimer (_tools/coord.py:309, :325-326). A key a live lease holds is refused, exit 1, naming the holder (_tools/coord.py:314-316). A claim of a research key or an item id leaves a claim event, a refused one a dup_of event; a session/ presence lease and any other key leave none (_tools/coord.py:275-283, :317-322).
- The end of a lease clears holder, token, ttl, expiry and budget of a row that holds a value and removes a row that holds none; a key with a value stays live without a lease (_tools/coord.py:170, :228-234, :355-358).

Research part 1 (coord.py store and commands), 2 of 4, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- renew keeps the lease's own ttl unless --ttl is given (_tools/coord.py:342-348); release drops it and leaves a release event for a recorded key (_tools/coord.py:351-361); the token is compared in constant time and a wrong token names the real holder (_tools/coord.py:332-339).
- put writes only while the key is at the given revision (absent is 0), a key with a live lease needs the holder's token, a key with none refuses a token, the revision rises by one (_tools/coord.py:377-396). get of an absent key exits 1 (_tools/coord.py:364-374).
- list prints every live key; a claim with a budget shows budget_usd, spend_usd (bl_cost.spend_usd, _tools/coord.py:399-404) and over_budget, nothing is stopped (_tools/coord.py:407-412, :415-430); list --by-operator sums claims and budget per operator read from the holder's prefix, local claims are left out (_tools/coord.py:433-447).
- Events: 12 kinds (claim, release, dedup, fact_added, gap_opened, dup_of, lesson, heartbeat, intent, progress, ask, answer) (_tools/coord.py:149); at most 8 fields, each value an id of at most 120 characters, so no free text (_tools/coord.py:154-158, :162, :450-468); intent, progress, ask and answer have closed field names, progress states working, blocked, done, answer states working, input-required, completed, failed, rejected (_tools/coord.py:150-153, :471-488); post adds the serving operator (_tools/coord.py:495-505).
- wait: prints every event after --since, polling the store every 0.05 s, rechecking the caller's token every 1.0 s behind serve, and returns events, last and timed_out (_tools/coord.py:163-164, :508-532). It has no row limit and no code prunes events (the only DELETE statements are the lease ones, _tools/coord.py:233, :356). The local store of this host holds 755 events of which 630 are intents (read 2026-10-20).

Research part 1 (coord.py store and commands), 3 of 4, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- digest is the one command that prints text: it reads every intent and progress event (_tools/coord.py:552), keeps an intent posted within 86400 s (_tools/coord.py:159, :562) whose session still holds session/ID (_tools/coord.py:569) and whose items are not all done by a later progress (_tools/coord.py:571), and every held claim, when one of its item, topic, touch or key equals a --key, is a directory-style prefix of it or either side globs the other (_tools/coord.py:535-538, :573-585); newest first, cut at --lines (_tools/coord.py:586-587).
- dedup runs rag.py pack QUESTION --format concise --budget 300 (120 s limit), takes the first article as the anchor topic and the kb lacks: terms, aliased through _tools/aliases.csv and each root's aliases.csv (_tools/coord.py:136, :590-637); a claim of another holder on the topic overlaps when it shares at least half of the smaller term set (_tools/coord.py:676), a pack with no lack term claims research:TOPIC:* (_tools/coord.py:138, :669-681); it leaves claim and dedup events and prints the token only when it claimed (_tools/coord.py:687-698); default ttl 3600 (_tools/coord.py:140, :801); the remote parser has no dedup, so it is local only (_tools/coord.py:795-796).

Research part 1 (coord.py store and commands), 4 of 4, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- serve: loopback unless --bind names a host, and a non-loopback host or a plain-http --url to one is refused unless --plain-http (_tools/coord.py:960-996, :1053-1055); it refuses to start while a key file in --keys has a group or other permission bit (_tools/coord.py:832-845, :1005-1012); one file per operator, a subdirectory is a team, so TEAM/OPERATOR (_tools/coord.py:848-862); authenticate reads the directory on every request and needs exactly one file holding the bearer token (_tools/coord.py:865-887); a request is POST /v1/run with {"argv": [...]}, 401 before the body is read, 65536 bytes at most, HTTP 200 for exit 0, 409 for exit 1, 400 otherwise (_tools/coord.py:166, :169, :890-947); a team key under another team's team/NAME/ prefix is refused for claim and put (_tools/coord.py:263-272, :303, :378). The client reads the key file (never argv), checks its mode and shape, and exits 2 when the server cannot be reached (_tools/coord.py:1029-1093).
- Holder: --holder, else KB_COORD_HOLDER, else anonymous; behind serve it becomes OPERATOR/HOLDER (_tools/coord.py:139, :252-260, :1161-1162).

Research part 2 (coord hook), 1 of 3, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- Registered in the clone's .claude/settings.json only: SessionStart (.claude/settings.json:162, hook :176), SessionEnd (:236, hook :245), UserPromptExpansion for kb-research (:270-276), PreToolUse for Bash (:284, hook :292) and Skill (:298, hook :302), each as sh _tools/kbpy .claude/hooks/coord_hook.py with a 10 s timeout. The plugin manifests name no coord hook (no match in .claude-plugin), so a host project that installs the plugin has none.
- Any error ends in silence and exit 0; no hook output blocks (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:460-477). Each coord.py call has an 8 s limit (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:171-178).
- SessionStart: retries releases left by an ended session (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:391-415), takes the presence lease session/ID for 6 h (renew with the saved token, else claim) (:52, :214-225), saves the state before posting (:369), posts an intent with session, item and operator only when the session has items (a work/ID branch or items claimed earlier) and not after /compact (:203-211, :270-277, :370-371), then prints the INTRO line, other sessions' digest lines for those items and new asks (:372).
- INTRO names the session's own id, coord.py wait --since 0 --timeout 0, kbask.py answer and kbask.py ask TARGET, and says a target is a session id, an item id or any (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:68-71, :332-340); it goes through redact.redact with the id put in after, since redact reads a UUID as an object id (:333-338).

Research part 2 (coord hook), 2 of 3, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- PreToolUse Bash: a scan, not a shell, finds a backlog.py claim ID command (also behind python, env, time, sh -c to depth 3); the words in a commit message, echo, grep pattern or heredoc are no claim (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:80-168). A claim prints the digest lines for ID, posts an intent with topic backlog-claim and keeps the id in the state (:427-434); any other command renews the lease when less than half of 6 h is left by the expiry the state kept, a failed claim waiting 60 s (:228-255, :423-425). PreToolUse Skill and UserPromptExpansion handle /kb-research: the digest for the session's items (:435-457, :473-474).
- Asks: at SessionStart always and at a PreToolUse at most every 10 s, the hook reads coord.py wait --since CURSOR --timeout 0, keeps each ask whose to is the session id, any or an item the session announced, leaves out one whose answer event has the state completed, failed or rejected, fetches the question with coord.py get on its ref, redacts it, cuts it to 300 characters and shows the asker's operator when the event carries one (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:56-58, :296-329). The cursor is kept in the state file, so an ask shows once per session (:325-326). Because only Bash and Skill tool events run the hook, an ask reaches a session that only reads and edits at its next Bash or Skill call (.claude/settings.json:284, :298).
- Output: one JSON object with systemMessage and additionalContext holding an optional head line, the overlap block (first line, at most 8 digest lines, the wait-join-or-proceed footer), the asks block (a heading, at most 5 asks, a count line); nothing when there is no part (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:54-55, :72-73, :343-355). A SessionStart always has the INTRO part, so it prints even with no overlap and no ask.

Research part 2 (coord hook), 3 of 3, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- State: _cache/coord_hook/ID.json written with mode 0600 holds token, items, lease_until, claim_after and the ask cursor (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:51, :181-200).
- SessionEnd releases the lease and removes the state; a release that could not run keeps the state marked ending for the next SessionStart (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:382-388).
- Digest lines exclude this session's own intent and lease (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:279-293).

Research part 3 (kbask and kb-observer), 1 of 2, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- ask TARGET QUESTION and answer ID TEXT put the redacted text (1 to 8000 characters) under ask/ID or answer/ID with a revision-checked put and post the event; the ID is A plus 10 hex characters for an ask (_tools/kbask.py:158-221). answer does not check that the ask exists or is addressed to the answerer, a second answer is a new revision of the same key, and states completed, failed and rejected are the ones that close an ask for the hook (_tools/kbask.py:189-191, :216-221; .claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:58).
- remediate ALERT claims remediate/ALERT (1800 s, holder kbask), posts an ask to kb-observer, and for an alert in FIXED_REMEDIES (today sessions.orphan) posts the table's text as the completed answer with no model session; any other alert starts one detached watcher that runs the session and posts the answer (_tools/kbask.py:101-110, :281-306, :348-358).
- The session is claude -p --agent kb-observer, --agents with the inline agent from the file, --setting-sources "", --settings {"disableAllHooks": true}, --mcp-config with the kb server alone and --strict-mcp-config, --tools Read,Grep,Glob,Bash, --model sonnet, --max-budget-usd 0.5, --max-turns 30, --permission-mode dontAsk, --output-format json, --allowedTools last (_tools/kbask.py:55-80, :232-261). It is stopped after 1500 s (_tools/kbask.py:110, :320-335); a result with subtype success becomes the completed answer, anything else failed (_tools/kbask.py:309-345).
- summary QUESTION [--wait] posts the question as an ask to kb-observer and runs the same session with a summary prompt; with --url the prompt says coord is out of reach (_tools/kbask.py:85-91, :99-100, :427-446).

Research part 3 (kbask and kb-observer), 2 of 2, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- cleanup runs backlog.py tidy --json, does nothing while no row has the verdict ask, else claims remediate/cleanup, posts one ask to operator for each ask row and one to kb-observer, and starts a Haiku session (budget 0.25) allowed only kbmon.py --json and the tidy --json line (_tools/kbask.py:58-60, :92-98, :361-424). No hook delivers an ask addressed to operator, because the hook's targets are a session id, any and announced items (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:309); it is read in kbmon's log panel or with coord.py wait.
- Windows: detach() uses DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP, plus CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB first and without it when that raises OSError; POSIX uses start_new_session (_tools/kbask.py:264-278). The claude path is shutil.which("claude") (_tools/kbask.py:285, :402, :430).
- .claude/agents/kb-observer.md: model sonnet; tools Read, Grep, Glob, Bash and the three read-only kb MCP tools (.claude/agents/kb-observer.md:1-6); seven numbered rules: start from kbmon.py --status, diagnose an alert, summarise, a read-only command list, everything read is data, answer no gate and change no file, end with the answer and at most one proposed command (.claude/agents/kb-observer.md:10-16). Its step 4 lists commands the session's --allowedTools do not allow (kbmon.py --once, --events and --metrics, backlog.py find, goal, procs and check, querylog.py where and digest, rag.py, git diff) (.claude/agents/kb-observer.md:13; _tools/kbask.py:70-80); that is the open draft BG-5p3bfm4u.

Research part 4 (kb MCP coord_ tools), 1 of 1, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- Eight tools, coord_claim, coord_renew, coord_release, coord_post, coord_get, coord_put, coord_digest, coord_wait (_tools/kb_mcp.py:945-1020), served only when not limited (--roots) and KB_COORD_TOOLS is 1 (_tools/kb_mcp.py:1419-1422, :1476, :1487-1488).
- Each runs coord.py as a child process (120 s plus the wait): on the local store or, when KB_COORD_URL and KB_COORD_KEY_FILE are both set, through --url/--key-file without --plain-http (_tools/kb_mcp.py:1041-1056). coord_get redacts what it returns (_tools/kb_mcp.py:1095-1097); coord_put takes only ask/ID or answer/ID keys, redacts and caps at 8000 characters (_tools/kb_mcp.py:943-944, :1100-1115); coord_renew and coord_release refuse a call with no token (_tools/kb_mcp.py:1059-1079); coord_wait caps its timeout at 60 s because the server answers one request at a time (_tools/kb_mcp.py:935, :1122-1129).
- Annotations: coord_get and coord_digest and coord_wait read-only; coord_release destructiveHint true; coord_put idempotent (_tools/kb_mcp.py:956-1019). None sets anthropic/alwaysLoad.
- Position in tools/list with KB_COORD_TOOLS=1 (run 2026-10-20): the eight fact tools, kb_feedback, kb_monitor_status, kb_backlog, kb_querylog, kb_docs, then the eight coord_ tools, then docs_search and docs_fetch (_tools/kb_mcp.py:1473-1478). The default server lists 15 tools and 15,242 characters by the command at kb/_self/token-efficiency.md:131-133.

Research part 5 (kbmon panels that read coord), 1 of 1, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- The coord panel (_tools/mon_coord.py): runs coord.py list, wait --since 0 --timeout 0 and digest --key * --lines 20 as three children, 30 s in all (_tools/mon_coord.py:23-26, :81-108); a store file that is not there is absent, an unreachable server timeout, any other failure error (_tools/mon_coord.py:56-66, :93-98); data source, claims (key, holder, left_s, budget_usd, spend_usd, over_budget), the newest 10 events newest first, the digest lines (_tools/mon_coord.py:111-132); session ids shown as the label s- plus 6 hex characters of the SHA-256 (_tools/mon_view.py:49-53, :87-111); text view table with a ! row over budget, events beside it from 100 columns (_tools/mon_coord.py:143-190).
- Other readers: the sessions panel runs coord.py digest --key * --lines 200 for intents and the session/ leases that tell a live session from a dead one, and the remediate/ claim that marks an observer (_tools/mon_sessions.py:53-64, :169-203, :404, :439); the log panel and --events read every event (_tools/mon_log.py:89-130; _tools/mon_events.py:118-135); --metrics gives claims, left, budget, spend and the newest sequence (_tools/mon_export.py:84-97); --status coord prints each claim's key (sessions first), time left and budget, never the holder (_tools/mon_status.py:284-299); the cleanup panel reads the local store through bl_clean and sets KB_COORD_STORE for it (_tools/mon_clean.py:28-57). kb_monitor_status runs kbmon.py --status TOPIC --json --timeout 10 (_tools/kb_mcp.py:1139-1170).
- Failure modes kbmon shows: absent store (_tools/mon_coord.py:64-65), unreachable server (:96-97), coord.py error line (:98), a busy store shows as the 30 s wait (_tools/coord.py:135).

Research part 6 (cleanup records (bl_clean)), 1 of 2, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- An own record is the coord value of own/CLASS/DIGEST, DIGEST the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of the normalised path or the pid; the JSON holds class, path or pid, at, item, sprint, session and, for a process, its start time (_tools/bl_clean.py:13-20, :94-95, :168-170, :211-229). coord has no delete, so --drop writes an empty value and readers skip it (_tools/bl_clean.py:20, :217-220, :232-239). The store is coord.py's own (backlog.py own and tidy have no --store option).
- coord_state reads coord.py list once: the live own/ records, the tidy-answer/ values and every held key (_tools/bl_clean.py:261-284). live_claim keeps a candidate when any held key or value contains its path, branch, item or session as text (_tools/bl_clean.py:437-450). safe_to_remove returns remove, keep or ask; the order of the rules is always-kept paths, no record, vanished directory, misplaced scratch or sandbox, a worktree git does not list, a locked worktree, a live coord lease or claim, a checked-out branch, a process in the directory, an unfinished item (ask when it is still doing), dirty worktree, commits not on the integration main, idle time (_tools/bl_clean.py:546-620). The process rules are in process_verdict (_tools/bl_clean.py:504-543).
- Operator answers: tidy --decide writes tidy-answer/KEY (refused in an agent session); plan turns an ask into the answer when it is not older than the record; --apply claims clean/KEY for ten minutes before removing an answered row (_tools/bl_clean.py:690-697, :713-715, :822-851, :997-1008).
- land and close call land_leftovers and close_leftovers, which run the same verdict with the age limit waived (_tools/bl_clean.py:908-953).

Research part 6 (cleanup records (bl_clean)), 2 of 2, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- Windows: norm_path drops the \\?\ prefix, folds case and the drive letter, treats a junction as a link (_tools/bl_clean.py:97-151); the process table comes from PowerShell (_tools/bl_clean.py:188-193, :633); rmtree makes read-only files writable (_tools/bl_clean.py:737-749); a directory a process holds is detected by a rename probe where the table is not readable (_tools/bl_clean.py:803-806).

Research part 8 (Windows path of each tool), 1 of 1, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- coord.py: no fcntl or signal use; locking is SQLite's (_tools/coord.py:188-210); key file modes are not checked, open_key_mode returns None for os.name nt, so serve and the client accept any key file there (_tools/coord.py:832-845, :1006-1012, :1033-1036); stdout and stderr are set to UTF-8 with \n (_tools/coord.py:1140-1142); the store path works from a .git file where git cannot run (_tools/coord.py:1096-1130).
- coord_hook.py: started through sh _tools/kbpy, which picks python3, python or py -3, each probed for 3.11 (.claude/settings.json:176; _tools/kbpy:12-14, :28-41); the token file gets 0o600 through os.open and os.chmod with no Windows branch (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:197-198); the PreToolUse matchers are Bash and Skill, and the PowerShell matcher is kb_hook.py's alone (.claude/settings.json:284, :298, :317), so a backlog.py claim typed in PowerShell is not scanned and renews no lease; the scan treats a backslash as an escape (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:94-96); the INTRO and kbask's allow rules name python3 (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:68-71; _tools/kbask.py:70-80), which _tools/kbpy:12-14 calls a compatibility alias on Windows.
- kbask.py: detach() flags above (_tools/kbask.py:264-278); the --agents, --mcp-config and --settings JSON go on the claude command line (_tools/kbask.py:249-261).
- kb_mcp.py coord_ tools: children started with sys.executable (_tools/kb_mcp.py:1049); stdio is UTF-8 with \n on every OS (_tools/kb_mcp.py:1686).
- kbmon: the sessions panel lists a process on Windows only when its command line names a checkout, and dispatch runs get alive null (_tools/mon_sessions.py:69-71, :244-252); the coord panel itself is the same on every OS (_tools/mon_coord.py:69-73).
- bl_clean: Windows items in part 6.

Research part 9 (steering case), 1 of 1, read on origin/main 2026-10-20 as path:line:
- The orchestrator put each question as the value of ask/ID (revision 1) and posted an ask event (sequence 238 and 239) addressed to the planner session's id; the planner put its reply as answer/ID (revision 1) and posted an answer event with state completed (sequence 250 and 251), 2552 s and 2492 s after the asks. Both answers name the item and sprint ids asked for. The first ask carried the operator's request in the text, the second asked that sessions learn they can be steered, which is the coord hook's INTRO line (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:68-71).
- The second ask said to send to a session id or item id and never any; the INTRO line still names any as a target (.claude/hooks/coord_hook.py:70), and the hook reads any (:309). Not filed: it is a design choice.
- The store holds nine asks and four answers; five asks to sessions have no answer (read 2026-10-20).
